Reusable Academic Paper Template

A Quarto Template with Numbered Citations

Authors
Affiliations

Alice Example

Example University

Bob Researcher

Example Institute of Technology

Abstract

This reusable Quarto template demonstrates a clean academic manuscript structure with automatic numbered citations, numbered bibliography entries, cross-references, equations, figures, and tables. Citations are written with standard Pandoc syntax, for example [@einstein1905], while the rendered PDF displays numeric square-bracket citations.

Keywords

Quarto, academic writing, numbered citations, reproducible research

Introduction

This document is a reusable academic Quarto template. It preserves the useful journal-style PDF functionality from the existing local Quarto extension while removing tutorial filler text.

Single citations use normal Pandoc syntax, as in (Einstein 1905). A second citation appears independently as (Shannon 1948). Multiple citations are also written normally, for example (Einstein 1905; Shannon 1948; Knuth 1984). The citation numbers and bibliography numbering are generated automatically during rendering.

Section references use Quarto cross-references. For example, Section 2 introduces the reproducible methods pattern used by this template.

Methods

Mathematical statements can be numbered and referenced. The mass-energy relation in Equation 1 is included as a compact example.

\[ E = mc^2 \tag{1}\]

Additional inline mathematics can be written as \(\alpha + \beta = \gamma\) without affecting equation numbering.

Results

Figures can be included with standard Markdown image syntax and a Quarto label. Figure 1 shows a placeholder figure that can be replaced with project-specific artwork.

Tables can be written directly in Markdown. Table 1 reports a small example dataset.

Discussion

The document demonstrates references to Section 1, Equation 1, Figure 1, and Table 1. The source remains editable as a normal .qmd manuscript, while Quarto and Pandoc handle numbering, citations, and bibliography generation.

This final sentence cites a fourth source (Lamport 1994) so that the bibliography demonstrates multiple automatically numbered entries.

References

Einstein, Albert. 1905. “Zur Elektrodynamik Bewegter körper.” Annalen Der Physik 322 (10): 891–921. https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19053221004.
Knuth, Donald E. 1984. The TeXbook. Addison-Wesley.
Lamport, Leslie. 1994. LaTeX: A Document Preparation System. 2nd ed. Addison-Wesley.
Shannon, Claude E. 1948. “A Mathematical Theory of Communication.” Bell System Technical Journal 27 (3): 379–423. https://doi.org/10.1002/j.1538-7305.1948.tb01338.x.

# Introduction {#sec-introduction}

This document is a reusable academic Quarto template. It preserves the useful journal-style PDF functionality from the existing local Quarto extension while removing tutorial filler text.

Single citations use normal Pandoc syntax, as in [@einstein1905]. A second citation appears independently as [@shannon1948]. Multiple citations are also written normally, for example [@einstein1905; @shannon1948; @knuth1984]. The citation numbers and bibliography numbering are generated automatically during rendering.

Section references use Quarto cross-references. For example, @sec-methods introduces the reproducible methods pattern used by this template.

# Methods {#sec-methods}

Mathematical statements can be numbered and referenced. The mass-energy relation in @eq-energy is included as a compact example.

$$
E = mc^2
$$ {#eq-energy}

Additional inline mathematics can be written as $\alpha + \beta = \gamma$ without affecting equation numbering.

# Results {#sec-results}

Figures can be included with standard Markdown image syntax and a Quarto label. @fig-placeholder shows a placeholder figure that can be replaced with project-specific artwork.

![Placeholder figure for the reusable paper template.](placeholder.png){#fig-placeholder width="55%"}

Tables can be written directly in Markdown. @tbl-example reports a small example dataset.

| Method | Accuracy | Runtime (s) |
|:-------|---------:|------------:|
| Baseline | 0.82 | 12.4 |
| Proposed | 0.91 | 10.8 |

: Example table with an automatically numbered caption. {#tbl-example}

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

The document demonstrates references to @sec-introduction, @eq-energy, @fig-placeholder, and @tbl-example. The source remains editable as a normal `.qmd` manuscript, while Quarto and Pandoc handle numbering, citations, and bibliography generation.

This final sentence cites a fourth source [@lamport1994] so that the bibliography demonstrates multiple automatically numbered entries.
